scope: Synthetic identifiability control for first scholarly question; no historical assignment or acoustic reconstruction.
inputs: Four distinct graphic slots with fixed identity and order, four distinguishable abstract sound labels, arbitrary bijective assignment. Every candidate preserves the same graphic record. No sound evidence initially.
derivation: After k independent fixed graphic-sound pairs there are (4-k)! bijections on the remaining labels. Exhaustive permutation counts below. With zero pairs every target slot admits every sound label. When actual systems allow null, multiple or context-dependent readings, this bijective control cannot be assumed as their ontology.
consequence: An alignment based only on shared graphic identity or position cannot discriminate competing sound assignments under these assumptions. Seek independently dated witnesses of pronunciation or contrast. A unique assignment of categorical labels still leaves acoustic realization unspecified.
exposure: No withheld historical targets inspected by this control.
